prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the camera wearer's forward progression from an indoor vestibule (~2–3 m from the double glass doors in frame 1) through the doorway (within arm's reach at <0.5 m in frames 3–4) and out onto an exterior walkway in frame 5. Outside, it resolves the ground plane receding into the parking lot, placing the rear of the left-hand U-Haul box truck (with its extended ramp) at roughly 8–10 m in frame 1 and closing to ~4–5 m on the left by frame 5, while the central white van sits roughly 5–7 m further back (~10–15 m from the wearer) with a lamppost and shrubbery to the right (~3–6 m). In frames 1–2, the depth map reveals the geometry of the completely dark interior walls and overhead ceiling that are nearly invisible in the underexposed RGB frames. However, the map is unreliable on the glass door panes: in frames 1–2 it treats the transparent glass as distant black voids while ignoring the exterior vehicles, and in frames 3–5 it blurs or erases distant background cars (>20 m) and the person standing beside the white van into the dark background sky.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates vehicles in the outdoor parking lot across the five frames, tracking the central white van (labeled 'truck', ~10–15 m away in front-center/right) and flanking parked sedans (labeled 'car', ~15–25 m away to the left and right) as the camera wearer approaches and exits the doorway. As the wearer clears the occluding door mullions in frames 4 and 5, the map newly segments the rear of the nearby U-Haul box truck on the left (~4–6 m away, labeled 'car'/unlabeled red mask on its ramp in frame 4 and 'truck' in frame 5) alongside additional distant cars (~20–30 m away) between the two trucks. In the early frames (1–3), the masks help separate the overlapping silhouettes of the white van and adjacent sedans seen through the narrow glass panes and door bars. However, the map is unreliable for non-vehicle scene elements and close structures: it completely misses the interior doors, frames, and walkway, fails to detect the person standing within arm's reach of the white van's open passenger-side door, and misclassifies the U-Haul truck and its ramp as 'car' instances in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely blank across all five frames, providing no body or hand skeleton detections anywhere in the scene. In the RGB strip, the camera wearer's own hands and arms remain below or outside the field of view even when pushing through the glass door within arm's reach (<0.5 m) in frames 3–4. The only visible person in the scene stands roughly 10–15 m away in the center-left parking lot, positioned within arm's reach of the white van's open side door and facing toward the van's interior rather than looking toward the camera wearer. Because this person occupies only a tiny cluster of pixels and is intermittently occluded by the door frame in frames 1–2 and 4, the pose estimator fails completely and offers no spatial information beyond confirming the absence of nearby, unoccluded figures.
